arguments.summary: Completed-session technical evidence is constructive but differentiated. NVDA has positive 5/21/63-session absolute returns, broad-market leadership at each window, and 63-session sector leadership, although it still lags XLK over 21 sessions. MU’s 21-session rebound remains strong and its 63-session return is positive, but it has slipped over five sessions, trails both comparators over that window, and carries much larger realized volatility and close-path drawdown. Historical regime frequencies are descriptive analogs only, not calibrated probabilities.

claims.text:
Matched SIP, split-adjusted, price-return comparisons through 2026-10-02 (percentage-point excess; instrument minus benchmark):
PAIR NVDA/SPY 5=+4.1671 21=+3.6656 63=+17.1931
PAIR NVDA/XLK 5=+2.1418 21=-4.5778 63=+10.7902
PAIR MU/SPY 5=-0.4611 21=+11.8413 63=+6.7098
PAIR MU/XLK 5=-2.4865 21=+3.5978 63=+0.3068

NVDA’s 2026-10-02 completed close was $233.95. Its 5/21/63-session returns were +3.9454%/+4.2511%/+19.6369%; the close stood 4.54%, 7.18% and 16.56% above the SMA20/50/200. Over the latest five sessions the SMA20 rose 0.9161%; the close was 1.3385% above the prior 21-session closing high. Last-session and recent-five-session volume were 1.3382x and 1.1189x the stated prior median, while the 63-session maximum close-path drawdown was -10.5835%. Annualized realized volatility was 14.88%/24.85%/38.25% over 5/21/63 sessions under the supplied close-to-close methodology.

NVDA shows absolute price-level strength and broad-market leadership: it beat SPY at 5, 21 and 63 sessions. Leadership versus technology is mixed rather than universal: it beat XLK over 5 and 63 sessions but lagged by 4.5778 points over 21 sessions. The move above the prior 21-session closing high with elevated volume supports a continuation interpretation, but one volume ratio does not establish sustained breakout confirmation. The competing explanation is a short-term rebound within technology-sector momentum rather than renewed leadership at every window.

MU’s 2026-10-02 completed close was $1,074.89. Its 5/21/63-session returns were -0.6828%/+12.4268%/+9.1536%; the close stood 4.87%, 12.43% and 57.70% above the SMA20/50/200. The SMA20 rose 3.1041% over five sessions, but the close remained 2.0503% below the prior 21-session closing high. Last-session and recent-five-session volume were 1.1404x and 1.2522x the prior median. Its 63-session maximum close-path drawdown was -25.4770%, and annualized realized volatility was 36.57%/49.55%/74.56% over 5/21/63 sessions.

MU’s recent pullback coexists with medium-window strength: it trailed SPY and XLK over five sessions, yet beat both over 21 sessions. Over 63 sessions it led SPY by 6.7098 points but only narrowly led XLK by 0.3068 point. The rising SMA20 and elevated recent volume support a rebound-continuation case, while failure to clear the prior 21-session closing high, very high 63-session volatility and a -25.4770% close-path drawdown make that continuation materially less stable than the level trend alone suggests.

The coarse current-regime analog (close above SMA20, SMA20 above SMA50, positive 21-session return) produced NVDA positive-forward-return frequencies of 58.1132%, 58.4906% and 71.6981% at 5/21/63 sessions versus unconditional rates of 58.8697%, 61.6954% and 73.4694% (265 conditional and 637 unconditional observations). MU’s corresponding frequencies were 59.1503%, 67.6471% and 79.0850% versus 57.9278%, 63.4223% and 71.1146% (306 conditional and 637 unconditional observations). These overlapping observations come from one finite 2023-12-18 to 2026-07-06 lookback; dependence, regime selection and lack of out-of-sample validation mean they are not calibrated probabilities, causal estimates or guarantees. NVDA’s conditional hit rates were slightly below its unconditional rates at all three windows, whereas MU’s were above, but that descriptive contrast does not establish forecast superiority.

The market was closed at assessment time, so the operative market-behavior anchors are the 2026-10-02 SIP completed closes. The latest NVDA IEX trade was $234 at 19:59:59.998859 UTC and no current quote was available; MU’s latest IEX trade was $1,074.71 at 19:59:58.451494 UTC and its displayed quote was a market-closed single-venue observation. IEX snapshots are neither consolidated nor executable current quotes.

For the 63-session technical mandate, NVDA currently has the cleaner observed path: stronger absolute return, much lower realized volatility and drawdown, and materially larger excess returns over both SPY and XLK. MU retains positive 63-session absolute performance and broad-market leadership, but its sector edge is marginal and its path risk is much greater. This is a technical comparison only, not a fundamental or valuation preference.

NVDA continuation case: holding above the frozen 2026-10-02 SMA50 while the recomputed 21-session NVDA-minus-XLK excess turns positive would pair price-level strength with restored sector leadership. Opposing path: a completed close below that frozen level while 21-session sector excess stays negative would weaken the breakout interpretation and indicate that absolute strength did not translate into durable relative leadership.

MU continuation case: maintaining the rising short-term average, clearing the prior 21-session closing high and preserving positive 63-session excess versus XLK would support continuation of the rebound. Opposing path: persistent five-session comparator lag followed by a completed close below the frozen 2026-10-02 SMA50 would characterize the move as a failed rebound with unusually high path risk.

gaps.description: The requested issuer-specialist check for any corporate action that could impair comparability of the split-adjusted series was still awaiting routing/response. This is nonblocking because the supplied technical panel explicitly uses one SIP feed, split-adjusted prices, matched dates and reconciled return conventions, but independent issuer confirmation would strengthen auditability.
No non-overlapping out-of-sample analog study was supplied. The historical regime frequencies therefore cannot support calibrated odds or a statistical ranking between NVDA and MU.

assumptions: All trend and relative-performance statements use completed sessions through 2026-10-02, SIP feed, split-adjusted prices and price returns; no later or incomplete bars are included.
The frozen SMA50 checkpoints are the dated 2026-10-02 levels, not future dynamic moving averages and not trade instructions.
A one-day volume ratio is descriptive; sustained follow-through requires later completed-session evidence.
Historical analog frequencies are treated only as dependent descriptive samples, not probabilities or expected returns.
arguments.counter_thesis: NVDA’s high RSI, move above a prior closing high and negative 21-session excess versus XLK could mark short-term extension rather than durable sector leadership. MU’s much larger volatility and drawdown, negative five-session excess versus both comparators and failure to clear its prior 21-session closing high could overwhelm its positive 21/63-session returns. A broad risk reversal could therefore invalidate both constructive level trends, with MU’s observed path historically less stable.

review_conditions.description: If NVDA records a SIP split-adjusted completed close below $218.2782, the frozen 2026-10-02 SMA50, treat the current multi-average uptrend as materially weakened and re-evaluate the continuation setup; this is a research checkpoint, not an order or a future dynamic average.

After at least five additional completed sessions, recompute NVDA-minus-XLK 21-session price-return excess on matched SIP, split-adjusted data. A sustained positive sign would confirm restored sector leadership; a nonpositive sign would keep the setup classified as absolute/broad-market strength without 21-session technology leadership.

If MU records a SIP split-adjusted completed close below $956.0457, the frozen 2026-10-02 SMA50, interpret the current rebound as materially weakened and increase emphasis on its high path risk; this is a research checkpoint, not an order or a future dynamic average.

After at least five additional completed sessions, recompute MU-minus-XLK 63-session price-return excess on matched SIP, split-adjusted data. A negative sign would erase the current marginal sector edge and weaken the mandate-horizon setup; sustained widening above +3 percentage points would make sector leadership more convincing.

question_effects.reason: The corporate-action comparability check was proposed but no specialist answer was available in this task. The explicit split-adjusted, matched-feed panel remains usable with that auditability limitation.

shared_exposures.mechanism: Both had positive 21- and 63-session absolute returns and closed above their SMA20/50/200 on 2026-10-02, so a common reversal in large-cap technology momentum could weaken both technical setups. This is a dated co-movement candidate, not proof of common causal exposure or a portfolio allocation recommendation.
shared_exposures.qualification: The fixed benchmark set is not market breadth. NVDA and MU differ substantially in relative-return signs and observed path risk, so the shared setup should not be treated as identical.

agent_report.work_summary: I analyzed the supplied completed-session SIP price series, exact matched-window comparison panel, technical path panel, historical regime-frequency panels and single-venue snapshots. I separated completed closes from market-closed IEX observations, checked every 5/21/63-session excess-return sign, and tied continuation/opposing paths to specific review rules.
main_conclusions: NVDA has positive absolute returns and SPY outperformance at all three windows, but its 21-session excess versus XLK remains negative despite positive 5- and 63-session sector excess.
MU’s 21-session rebound is strong, but five-session relative performance is negative against both SPY and XLK and its 63-session XLK edge is only +0.3068 point.
NVDA’s 63-session realized volatility and maximum close-path drawdown are materially lower than MU’s, making NVDA’s observed trend cleaner on this technical evidence.

Conditional historical frequencies are not forecast probabilities; NVDA’s were below its own unconditional rates at all three windows, while MU’s were above, subject to overlapping-sample and regime-selection limitations.
No current consolidated executable quote was available; completed 2026-10-02 SIP closes are the proper anchors.
agent_report.short_summary: NVDA’s completed-session setup is the cleaner 63-session trend, though 21-session technology leadership has not been restored. MU’s rebound remains constructive but is more fragile because near-term relative performance weakened and observed volatility/drawdown are much larger.
limitations: The historical regime samples overlap and are not out-of-sample or probability-calibrated.
One volume ratio cannot confirm sustained accumulation or breakout follow-through.
IEX snapshots are single-venue, market-closed observations, not consolidated executable quotes.
